recipes.name: Black-Eyed Peas with Pork and Greens
ingredients_raw: 1 pinch cayenne pepper, or to taste
1 (10 ounce) can diced tomatoes with green chile peppers
1 bunch kale, ribs removed and leaves torn into pieces

steps.text: Place black-eyed peas into a large container and cover with several inches of cool water; let stand, 8 hours to overnight. Drain and set aside.

Cook pork neck bones and bacon in a Dutch oven over medium heat until lightly browned, about 5 minutes. Add onion, celery, and carrot; cook and stir until softened, 6 to 7 minutes. Stir in garlic and cook 1 minute.

Pour cold water and black-eyed peas into pork mixture; increase heat to high. Stir in bay leaf, thyme, cumin, black pepper, and cayenne pepper; bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 45 minutes.
Stir in tomatoes with green chile peppers and salt. Simmer uncovered until beans are tender, about 40 minutes.
Remove neck bones; separate any meat from bones, return meat to the Dutch oven, and discard bones.
Stir in diced ham and kale; cook until greens are tender, 10 to 15 minutes. Serve over rice.

raw_recipe.headline: Black-Eyed Peas with Pork and Greens
raw_recipe.description: This hearty pork and black-eyed peas with greens recipe is Chef John's variation of Hoppin' John. Perfect on New Year's Day or any time of the year!

review.reviewBody: I've made this soup several times . We love it. I ran out of time today, so I made this soup in my pressure cooker. I cooked the bacon and veggies right on the stove top in the pressure cooker. Then I added the soaked beans, spices, ham, diced tomatoes, spices and water just before I closed the lid. Easy prep. I brought the soup up to pressure and cooked for 10 minutes, took it off and let it set until the pressure cooker had depressurized: another 10 to 15 minutes. I added the kale immediately after opening the cooker and 10 minutes later we were eating soup. For those of you who have never tried pressure cooking, it ROCKS! The flavor of the soup was even better this time, and the unexpected company raved over it. Their 13 year old had two bowlfuls. By the way, I used Farmlands spiral ham and pieces instead of ham steaks. It's cheaper and has a much richer flavor.

Made this today and it was absolutely delicious. Didn't have Kale, so I used a half bag of collard greens that I had left over from another dish - guess any greens will do. I'm giving a lot to friends so they can see how good black-eyed peas and pork neck bones taste. Will definitely make this again.

This was crazy good. I used ham hocks instead of necks, and added andouille sausage to it with the kale. I did not have the canned tomatoes with peppers, so used fresh chopped tomatoes and some ground dried chiles. YUM!!

Excellent! Couldn't get any pork neck bones, so I substituted ham hocks instead. Next time I'll skip the bacon, increase the ham, and use ham hocks again, because their smoky flavor adds so much to this dish. Also used my slow cooker--two hours on high, then about five hours on low, adding the ham and kale during the last 45 minutes of cooking. 

Since I am allergic to cayenne, I used Penzey's Aleppo Pepper instead. I also doubled the amount of onion the recipe calls for, and sautéed the onion/celery/carrots before adding them to the slow cooker, in order to control the amount of liquid that the onions throw off. 

I can see this being my family's New Years Day dish for a long time!

Because I've never made black eyed peas (or any beans from scratch), this recipe looked really overwhelming to me, but it was the exact opposite. It was so easy!! I originally planned to make it in my crock pot, but I'm so glad I stayed with the suggested dutch oven. This is absolutely delicious and has a deep depth of flavor!! I would not change a thing!! I didn't have pork neck bones, but I did have ham shanks, so I used those instead, and the meal literally fell right off the bones! Thanks for sharing!

I followed the recipe except I didn't soak the black eyed peas. I read that the only advantage to soaking was that it reduced cooking time by up to an hour. So I just added the dry beans and monitored the mixture until the peas were nice and creamy. It was delicious, though I don't think I'll use smoked neck bones again because despite my best efforts there were still a few bone fragments in the final stew. Next time I'll use smoked ham hocks.

Delicious!! The Kale is a WAY WAY better recommendation than the greens I've used in the past. We subbed the 6 cups of water with 6 cups of organic chicken stock, and added an additional 2 cups of water to make the peas more soupy. Rather than the pork neck and bacon... I used the leftover spiral cut ham and bone from Christmas. Let that leg bone cook with the first half of the boil. We only had about 1.5 lbs of leftover ham.... it was perfect.

I definitely recommend this recipe .
I loved this recipe, but I changed it a bit. No tomatoes, only pork belly, spinach and used instant pot for 50 minutes and it was fabulous!

Great recipe. Followed it except for the following: Did not brown the pork neck bones. Seems redundant and does not add flavor as they are already smoked. Instead I boiled them until the meat came off the bones and used the broth instead of the water—just had to top it off with a small amount of water. Maybe the recipe was for raw neck bones? Never even looked in the store for raw one. I also had bacon already cooked so just chopped it up and added. I used smoked boneless pork chops instead of ham because that’s what I had. I think they are meatier and have more flavor. I put everything in a slow cooker except the kale and ham and cooked on high about 4 hours until peas were tender then added kale and ham and cooked until greens were tender. This is the first time I used smoked pork neck bones. It will not be the last. I think they have more flavor and less fat than ham hocks.

My favorite Hoppin' John so far! I had to go to three stores to find neck bones (they had both fresh and smoked - glad I got the smoked!). I was running out of time to get the family fed, so after about 45 minutes of simmering, I put the final ingredients with it into the InstantPot for 15 minutes. I used baby kale which was very tender, so I just added it at the last minute as I served over rice. I added one chicken bouillon cube during simmering because I was a little worried that using water instead of stock would make it less flavorful, but it was fantastic. The peas were creamy and perfectly cooked. My 8-year-old son, whose name happens to be John, announced that hopping John loves Hoppin' John! :)

This tasted way better than I expected, but also did some tweaking. I didn't want to wait on the beans over night so I prepped them in the pressure cooker. This greatly saved my cooking time since I didn't need all those simmering times. My family was grossed out by the thought of pigs feet or necks, so I substituted 1/3lb of pork sausage instead. I followed the rest per directions. We all actually enjoyed it quite well though. The recipe as written is quite labor some, so I'm glad I prepped the beans to save time.
My husband is from the south and he really enjoyed this version of black eye peas.
We had some left over BBQ ribs which worked well as a sub for the ham hocks and pretty much followed the recipe to spec. A very good hearty and tasty way to kick off the New Year.
I make this dish every New Year Day, My family loves it. The only thing I change is I use collard greens. A staple in the Thames household.

Made it according to the recipe, only I added some Hatch green chilis and instead of smoked ham (didn't have any), just increased the amount of the pork neck bones by 1/4 lb. Used Porkbelly instead of bacon and WOW! What a wonderful dish this is! It turned out larger than expected, but we have been eating the left-overs for a couple days now and it only seems to get better as it sits in the fridge! Only drawback is that we have found a couple of small bones from the pork. None on the first night where we served to company, but on following nights as we get towards the bottom of the leftovers. I will know to be more careful when seperating the meat next time. NOTE: Made and served with rice, but in following days, have been eating it by itself and enjoyed it even more. Turns out, the rice is overkill! Overall - DELICIOUS. Will make this again, for sure!

Wow this was delicious! Throwing away the other black eyed peas recipe from this site because this one is way better. Made exactly as written except I used leftover spiral hambone instead of pork neck bone. Oh my gosh sooo good. Lots of flavor and all the cooking times worked perfectly for me. Will become a New Years tradition from now on! Thanks Chef John!

I made this for our New Year's supper. Absolutely perfect! I followed the ingredients list and instructions exactly, no deviation. The pinch of cayenne adds such a nice zing. This will be our traditional Hoppin' John recipe from now on. YUM! The photo is my husband's third helping, lol!
Very Tasty... right down to the last pop ion your mouth of the black eyed peas...

I’ve never been a huge black-eyed pea fan but wanted to make the traditional dish w collards for NYD. So glad I chose this one bc turns out I do like black eyed peas! I didn’t read the directions that closely & basically omitted the first step involving the bacon & neck bones. Essentially followed the remainder of the recipe except I used a bag of frozen BEP & used 3 c chicken broth w 3 c water. Added the diced ham in when I added the beans & broth. Used the suggested spice measurements and they were spot on for our family- not hot but definitely a nice flavor. Added collards towards the end and in the last 15 min added the salt. Cooked the day before to really let the flavors meld. Impressed! Thank you Chef John!
Good recipe. Black eyed peas resemble cowrie shells which were used as currency in West Africa may be the reason for the belief that black eyed peas bring wealth.
